subject: Ironclad: Executive war-room playbook & customer update
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@ironclad.ai>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: priya.rao@ironclad.ai
Date: 2026-09-30T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Production spike — 30% latency increase + 500 errors across /generate

Sean —

We started seeing a sustained latency spike around 07:40 PT and a rising number of 500 responses on the /generate endpoint. Impact is visible in our staging and prod traffic; roughly 25–30% of requests are delayed beyond our 1.5s target and error rate jumped to ~3.8% this morning. Customers are noticing.

Can Redwood confirm if there was a rollout or infra change? We need a status and ETA for mitigation — this is affecting critical flows for two of our top accounts (billing and OCR ingestion).

I can provide traces if helpful (we pulled a handful and attached).

— Daniel
Daniel Park
CTO — Ironclad
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-30T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production spike — 30% latency increase + 500 errors across /generate

Team — putting an exec-level war-room together and looping in Ops + CS. Summary of ask from Ironclad attached (see traces). Immediate objectives:

1) Triage root cause and implement mitigation (15-min cadence updates).
2) Provide Ironclad a clear public-facing status and ETA within 30 minutes.
3) If unable to stabilize within 90 minutes, propose fallbacks (routing to ded-variant, reduce max tokens, turn on KV caching aggressively).

Owners:
- Grace: Triage runtime/kernel and confirm whether any model variant rollouts or kernel swaps occurred in the last 2 hours.
- Marcus: Prepare capacity plan (burst to Dedicated pools + preemptive routing) and estimate cost/impact.
- Laura: Draft an external-facing status note for Ironclad and coordinate with CS.
- Karthik: Pull telemetry and SLO graphs, prepare talking points for execs.
- Monica: Open the bridge, create channel #warroom-ironclad, and collect logs into the Drive folder.

I will brief Sales and the customer execs after the first triage update. Attachments: debug-trace-logs-20260930.zip (received from Ironclad).

— Sean
Sean Gallagher
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-30T08:36:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Re: Production spike — 30% latency increase + 500 errors across /generate

Update (08:36 PT) — preliminary triage:

- No config change found in control plane; no model rollout in the past 6 hours.
- Kernel-level telemetry shows an increase in token decode backpressure on one of the inference pods (pod-a1) — sustained queue growth coincident with Ironclad's trace timestamps.
- Error pattern: 500s originate from OOM retries in the runtime when sequence length spikes + concurrent KV cache misses.

Immediate mitigations executed (08:34 PT):
- Drained pod-a1 and replaced with a fresh instance running with conservative memory headroom.
- Enabled aggressive KV cache warming for the affected routing key (testing shows initial 40% reduction in tail latency on test traffic).
- Triggered short-term routing to warm standby variant (quantized variant q1) for low-latency traffic; this will increase token cost slightly but keeps throughput.

Next steps: Marcus to estimate burst capacity for 30 minutes of routing to Dedicated and Karthik to run SLO regression. I will continue to monitor and post at 08:50 PT.

— Grace
Grace O'Connor
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-30T08:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Re: Production spike — 30% latency increase + 500 errors across /generate

08:44 PT — Capacity & routing update:

- We have pre-warmed two Dedicated slots (d-pool-3) and can route up to ~4k rps with headroom for 20 minutes. Cost impact estimate: ~$1.6k incremental for the burst window.
- Recommendation: authorize routing 40% of Ironclad's traffic to Dedicated for the next 45 minutes while Grace stabilizes pod memory pressure.
- If Ironclad approves, we should also temporarily relax batching (smaller batch size) for their API key to reduce tail latency — minimal customer-visible change beyond cost.

I'll stand by for approval. Laura, once you have a draft status note, we should mention the Dedicated burst option as an immediate mitigation.

— Marcus Lin
Director, Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@ironclad.ai>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@ironclad.ai>
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-30T09:01:00-07:00
Subject: Status update — Ironclad incident (08:34 PT mitigations in progress)

Daniel / Priya —

Thanks for flagging this. Quick status from Redwood: we detected elevated tail latency and an uptick in 500s tied to memory pressure on a single inference pod. Actions taken so far (live):

- Replaced the affected pod and increased memory headroom.
- Enabled aggressive KV cache warming and routed a portion of traffic to a warmed quantized variant (q1) to reduce tail latency.
- We have pre-warmed Dedicated capacity as a contingency. If you approve, we can route up to 40% of your live traffic to that pool while we finish stabilization. Expected customer-visible impact: latency should return to baseline for most flows within ~15–30 minutes; some heavy long-sequence jobs may still queue for a short time.

Next update in 30 minutes or sooner if anything changes. If you want a private bridge, we can join immediately — Sean is maintaining the executive bridge.

Attachments: war-room-runbook-v1.pdf (operational steps we are following).

— Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Success Operations, Redwood Inference
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Ironclad Execs <cteam@ironclad.ai>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-01T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Executive summary & post-mortem plan — Ironclad incident (resolved)

Executive brief —

Status: Resolved (final remediation completed 2026-10-01T13:15 PT). Impact window: 07:40–12:50 PT on 2026-09-30. Root cause: intermittent KV cache miss amplification combined with a pod-level memory regression under long-sequence traffic leading to OOM retries and 500s.

What we did:
- Immediate pod replace + memory headroom increase (mitigated the OOMs).
- Short-term routing to quantized variant (q1) and aggressive KV cache warming reduced tail latency within 30 minutes.
- Burst routed 35% of Ironclad traffic to pre-warmed Dedicated capacity for ~90 minutes to buy stabilization time.
- Collected traces & logs and assembled the war-room runbook; key artifacts uploaded to Drive.

Customer-facing commitments we will follow up on by EOD:
1) Detailed post-mortem with timeline & remediation plan.
2) SLO credit proposal for the impacted window (draft in HubSpot deal IC-4521).
3) A proposed sustained config change to prevent recurrence: improve KV cache prefetch heuristics + add pod-level memory headroom guard.

Owners for the post-mortem: Grace (technical root cause + remediation), Marcus (capacity/cost accounting), Karthik (SLO analysis & graphs), Laura (customer comms + credits), Sean (exec liaison).

Thanks for the partnership and patience — we will share the post-mortem and a short exec slide deck by EOD.

— Sean Gallagher
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
